subject: Is the bioconductor version the latest?

messages.author: 9b48f0bcd1ff214c
messages.subject: Is the bioconductor version the latest?
parts:
Hello
I have a possibly silly question...
Where do I get the latest version of MethylKit?

I see the github page has only version 0.99 from 2016.
Bioconductor for R 4.3 has version 1.24.
Is the bioconductor version the latest? Where can If find out what the latest version is?

I ask because I am having a bunch of problems that I think may have been resolved long ago...
like when I try to run the correlation function, I cannot change the method to anything other than Pearson or it gives an error, stating that Pearson should be used but the manual says that spearmans is an option.

Regards
Ryan

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: Is the bioconductor version the latest?
parts:
Hi Ryan,

The version on Bioconductor is the latest. 
We did not set automated releases on github, that's why there we still have the version from 2016.

If you are having issues with the latest version, it would be great if you could post them on github together with a small reproducible example.

Best,
Alex

parts: I think the 'pearson' and 'spearman' correlation issue was because of the object class. I see now that the manual says that for 'methylBaseDB' only the pearson correlation is available. So I guess this means that if we have very large datasets we need to do some pre-processing to reduce the size of the data to allow it to be read into memory as a methylbase object if we want to use spearmans rank.

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: Is the bioconductor version the latest?
parts:
Hi Ryan,

Yes, you are right this is a bug. I opened an issue on our GitHub (https://github.com/al2na/methylKit/issues/280), but do currently not have the time to work on this. 

To get this working you may use run this code prior to calling the function, which is essentially the fix that I will upload soon: 

```
setMethod("getCorrelation", "methylBaseDB",
          function(object,method = c("pearson", "kendall", "spearman"),plot,nrow=2e6){
           
            if(is.null(nrow)){
             
              meth.fun <- function(data, numCs.index, numTs.index){
               
                data[, numCs.index]/( data[,numCs.index] + data[,numTs.index] )
              }
              meth.mat = methylKit:::applyTbxByChunk(object@dbpath,return.type = "data.frame",
                                         FUN = meth.fun, numCs.index = obj...@numCs.index,
                                         numTs.index = obj...@numTs.index)
            }else{
              data = methylKit:::headTabix(object@dbpath,nrow=nrow,return.type = "data.frame")
              meth.mat = data[, obj...@numCs.index]/( data[,obj...@numCs.index] +
                                                        data[,obj...@numTs.index] )
            }
           
            names(meth.mat)=obj...@sample.ids
           
            method <- match.arg(method)
            print( cor(meth.mat,method=method) )
           
            if(plot) {
              methylKit:::.plotCorrelation(meth.mat = meth.mat,
                               title = paste(object@context, object@resolution ,method,"cor."),
                               method = method)
            }
          }  
)
```

Best,
Alex
